messages.content: the first and last pages of a book have the same picture of a house. does that mean nothing happened in the story?
no. the same picture can come before and after many things. the people may return to the house after a journey, or see it in a different way by the end.
make a short example where someone comes home after learning something.

a girl leaves her house because she wants to see the garden in another town. she learns that it took many people to make it and keep it growing. when she comes home, she looks at the small garden by her own door. she asks her family if they can work on it together. the house is the same, but she has a new idea for what to do there.
what changed if the house did not?
the girl learned something and came home with a new plan. a story can change what a person knows or wants without changing every object around them.
can the last picture mean home instead of nothing happened?
yes. with that story, the last picture can show that she is home again. what happened before it helps us understand the picture.
say it simply.
the last picture can show that she is home again. what happened before it helps us understand the picture.
my friend sent a long message, but i only see one question at the end. should i answer every sentence as if it were a question?
no. some sentences tell you what happened, rather than ask something. answer the question and use the other details to understand it.
answer in fewer words.
no. answer the question, using the rest of the message as context.
the question is can we meet after lunch. the message also says they will be at the library.
then you can answer about meeting and the place together: yes, i can meet after lunch. shall we meet at the library?
i cannot meet after lunch. i am free before lunch.
then say: i am not free after lunch, but i could meet before lunch. would that work for you?
can you ask about the place without saying i will come for sure?
would meeting at the library before lunch work for you?
does asking that choose the time for both of us?
no. it gives a possible time and place for your friend to answer.
write a story where a child stops in the middle of a song because she wants to hear someone else. do not make her sad.

a child has a song in mind while drawing at a table. her aunt comes into the room and starts the next part of the song. the child stops and listens because she does not know those words. when her aunt finishes, the child asks her to sing that part again slowly. she wants to learn it. soon they sing together, with the aunt helping when a word is new.
make the first part simple.
a child has a song in mind while drawing at a table. her aunt comes in and starts the next part. the child stops to listen because she wants to learn the words.
did her choice to stop mean she no longer liked the song?
no. she stopped so she could hear the part she did not know. listening was part of learning the song, rather than giving it up.
say the last answer simply.
she still liked the song. she wanted to hear and learn the new part.
now write a question she can ask after they sing together.
could we sing it once more so i can try the new part myself?
my room has a window on the north wall and a door on the south wall. if i look at the window, is the door behind me?
if you stand between the window and door and look north at the window, the south door is behind you. where you stand and which way you look are important.
make it simple.
if you stand between the window and door and look north at the window, the door is behind you.
what if i turn around to look at the door?
then the window is behind you. the places of the window and door have not changed. only the way you are looking has changed.
can you say that in two short sentences?
the window and door stay in the same places. you change which one is in front of you by turning around.
write a small story with a child learning that.
a child looked at the north window and said the door was behind him. he turned to look at the south door, then asked where the window went. his sister said it was still there, now behind him.
keep that story in the past, but make it shorter.
a child turned from the window to look at the door. his sister said the window had not moved. it was now behind him.
i came to help with a garden, but some work was already done. i feel like i came too late to do anything useful.
you can ask what is still needed. some work being done does not mean every part is finished. there may be another task, or the group may want help keeping the garden ready later.
what can i ask without choosing a task myself?
what would be useful for me to do now?
they say the flowers are ready, but the vegetable part needs work. i do not know how to start.
you can ask someone to show you one part first. you do not need to know what to do before asking to learn.
write a request for help.
could you show me what to do first in this part of the garden?
if someone helps me learn, are they the only person helping?
no. they help you learn, and you can then do part of the work. both can be useful to the group.
say it simply.
they help you learn, and you do part of the work. both are useful to the group.
if i say i wrote the letter myself, does that mean i was alone in the room?
no. myself can tell us who did the writing. other people could still be in the room without writing the letter for you.
make a small example with my sister reading near me.
i wrote the letter myself while my sister read a book at the other end of the table. she was there, but she did not write it for me.
ask my request simply.
make a small example with my sister reading near me.
what if she helped me choose the first word?
then you can say that you wrote the letter with a little help from your sister. you still did most of the writing, but she gave help with one part.
can i say she wrote the whole letter?
not if she only helped with the first word. that would say she did more than the part you gave her.
answer simply.
no. helping choose one word is not the same as writing the whole letter.
a person in my story is sad, but i enjoyed reading the story. is that wrong?
no. you can enjoy a story even when you do not like every hard thing that happens to its people. you may enjoy the writing, the ideas, or understanding the people better.
can you make an example about a person who wants to see a friend?
a person in a story wants to see a friend who lives far away. you can enjoy reading about them and still want them to be happy.
make that idea simple.
you can like reading about the person and still wish they could see their friend.
if i like the book, does that mean i want to live the same life?
no. a story can be good to read without being a life you would choose for yourself.
use good to read in a shorter answer.
a story can be good to read even when you would not want that life yourself.
ask me a question about what i liked, not whether i was sad.
what part of the story did you enjoy most?
a shop has an open window but a closed door and a note saying it is closed. can i say the shop is open because of the window?
not in the same meaning. the window can be open while the shop is closed to people coming in to buy things. open is about different things in those sentences.
write a short conversation at the door.
the window is open. can we go in? the note says the shop is closed. then the window does not mean they are ready for people? that is right. we should use the information on the note about the shop.
does the note say when it will open again?
not from the words you gave. it only says that the shop is closed.
what can i say to my friend without making up an hour?
the shop is closed, and i do not know when it will open again.
what if we see a worker inside?
you could ask if it is okay to speak with them, but seeing a worker does not by itself mean the shop is open for people to come in.
can the worker be working while the shop is closed?
yes. a person can do work inside before or after the time when people can come in to buy things.
i know which book i want, but i cannot remember its color. does that mean i do not know anything about it?
no. you may know its name or story even if you do not remember the color.
say it simply.
not knowing one detail does not mean you know nothing.
i remember it was about a woman learning to cook with her father. i do not know the name either.
then you know a part of the story. that may help you ask someone about it, though it may not be enough to find only one book.
write a request using only what i know.
i am looking for a book about a woman learning to cook with her father. i do not remember its name or color. could you help me find it?
should i add that the father is old?
only if you remember that detail. you have not said it yet, so adding it could send the person looking for a different story.
what if i am not sure?
you can say you are not sure rather than making the detail sound known.
change i will call after lunch to say i will call before lunch, without changing anything else.
i will call before lunch.
what changed in the meaning?
before lunch puts the call first and lunch later. after lunch puts lunch first and the call later.
say it in fewer words.
before puts the call first. after puts lunch first.
now make it a question to my sister.
can i call you before lunch?
does can i call you before lunch say she is free then?
no. it asks her about that time. she still needs to answer before you know whether it works for her.
she says after lunch is better. i can do that. write the reply.
after lunch works for me too. i will call you then.
what does then mean in that reply?
it is about the time after lunch that you both just chose.
my cousin kept a drawing i did not finish. i thought nobody would want it because part of the page is empty.
a drawing that is not finished can still have something a person likes. your cousin may like the part you drew or remember the time when you made it.
use not finished in a short answer.
a drawing that is not finished can still be something a person enjoys.
i want to ask what they like without saying they should not keep it.
you could ask: what do you like about this drawing?
they say it helps them remember our time in the garden. i forgot we made it there.
the drawing helps them remember being with you in the garden. the empty part does not take away that memory.
say it simply.
the drawing helps them remember your time together. it does not need to be finished to do that.
can i ask whether they want me to finish it?
you can ask whether they would like that. they may want to keep it as it is, so ask before changing it.
say my last question simply.
can i ask whether they want me to finish it?
picoboi, put it in a sentence.
what word or idea would you like me to put in a sentence?
i was thinking of unless, but i did not say it.
then a useful example is: i will read outside unless there is rain.
why did you not just know the word i had in mind?
you had not given it in the conversation. i should ask which word you want, rather than choose one and say that was the word you gave.
say it simply.
you did not tell me which word. asking helped me answer the request you really had.
now make a different sentence with unless, about a visit.
i will visit my aunt tomorrow unless she is busy.
does that say she is busy?
no. it says that her being busy could change the plan. it does not tell us yet whether she is busy.
make it shorter without changing that meaning.
i will visit tomorrow unless she is busy.
